name: Developmental Biology (PhD)

rules.name: Requirements Overview
rules.desc:
Graduate Degrees describes university requirements for the PhD degree.
The graduate program in Developmental Biology leads to the PhD degree. The department also participates in the Medical Scientists Training Program (MSTP), in which individuals are candidates for both the MD and PhD degrees.

rules.name: Course Requirements
rules.desc:
Students are required to complete at least five courses, including:

• DBIO 210

• DBIO 215

• An advanced graduate course in genetics or genomics

• An advanced graduate course in cell biology or biochemistry

• A course in quantitative or computational biology

children.name: Graduate Research
children.desc:
Students are required to complete a minimum of 135 units to graduate.
Students can adjust the units of their Graduate Research course (DBIO 399 or GENE 399) to 10 units per quarter (before reaching TGR) or 3 units per quarter (after advancing to TGR) to reach 135 units.

children.name: An advanced graduate course in genetics or genomics
An advanced graduate course in cell biology or biochemistry
A course in quantitative or computational biology

rules.name: Seminars and Journal Clubs
rules.desc: Students are expected to attend Developmental Biology seminars and journal clubs.

rules.name: Qualifying Exam
rules.desc: Completion of a qualifying examination is required for admission to PhD candidacy. The examination consists of an off-topic proposal on a subject different from the dissertation research.

rules.name: University Oral Examination
rules.desc: The student must pass the University Oral Examination, taken only after substantially completing their research. The examination is preceded by a public seminar in which the candidate presents the research. A dissertation reading committee conducts the oral examination.

rules.name: PhD Dissertation
rules.desc: The final requirements of the program include the presentation of a PhD dissertation as the result of independent investigation and constituting a contribution to knowledge in the area of developmental biology.

reviewNotes: The audit checks the 135 graduate units (your DBIO 399 or GENE 399 research units count toward them) and DBIO 210 and DBIO 215. You check by hand the other three required courses (an advanced graduate course in genetics or genomics, one in cell biology or biochemistry, and one in quantitative or computational biology), seminar and journal club attendance, the qualifying exam, the University Oral Examination and the dissertation.
